kinds.definition: The method drawn as an ordered sequence of stages (data collection or synthesis, filtering, training, retrieval, inference, verification) joined by arrows that hand data or artifacts from one stage to the next. Boxes are named by what they do, so the reader learns the order of operations and which stage is new. Models appear as black-box blocks or icons inside a stage rather than being opened up.

variants.definition: A single row (or column) of titled stages from input to output, possibly with one loop-back arrow; the default form.
Stacked bands or panels for phases that share components: training vs inference, pre-training vs fine-tuning, offline vs online, synthetic vs real data.
A dataset or benchmark being built: sources, then filtering, annotation and verification, then the dataset and sometimes its downstream uses; funnels, counts and one example record.
The method is a cycle (generate-verify-correct, evolve-score-select, act-store-train), drawn as a circle or as iteration snapshots with a dominant feedback arrow.
A shared pipeline or model fans out to several tasks, applications or analyses (or fans in from several domains), each branch ending in an example.
A classic flowchart with ovals, process boxes and decision diamonds, read top-down.

kinds.definition: The inside of a learned model: encoders, layers, attention and fusion blocks, heads and loss terms wired together, with tensors, tokens or embeddings flowing between them. The reader learns what the model is built from, what is shared, frozen or trained, and where the new component plugs in.

variants.definition: One diagram from the input sample through the modules to heads, outputs and losses.
Parallel encoders per modality, view or scale merged by a fusion block or a shared model.
The overall network plus an enlarged inset or lettered sub-panels showing the new block's internals.
The training objective is the structure: views, encoders and embeddings wired to several loss terms (contrastive, teacher-student, distillation).
One block repeated over time steps, layers, devices or diffusion steps and drawn as a chain.

kinds.definition: Two or more alternatives drawn in the same visual grammar and placed in parallel lanes or panels so that the difference is the message: prior vs proposed approach, naive vs fixed pipeline, a family of design variants, or several methods' outputs on the same input. The reader compares across lanes instead of following one path.

variants.definition: Two or three lanes drawing the same pipeline or block, prior or naive vs proposed, stacked or side by side.
Three or more sibling schematics of alternative designs or strategies, labelled (a)-(d) with the proposed one last; sometimes compressed into a check/cross feature table.
The same input processed by several methods, with the outputs (images, filmstrips, learned trees, chat answers) aligned for comparison.
One or more panels diagnose a failure or its cause on an example, followed by the remedy.

kinds.definition: One concrete run of the method: a specific instance (an image, a graph, a CPU cache, a conversation, a GUI session) is followed through numbered steps and redrawn after each, so the reader watches the method act on real or toy values. The instance is the protagonist; operations shrink to arrow labels or small boxes.

variants.definition: The same object is redrawn after each step at the same position and scale, with only the change highlighted.
An agent or model run shown with its real inputs and outputs: screenshots, frames, tokens or text turns.
Characters or icons act out a story in steps, such as an attack or a behavioural-study protocol.
The same update is drawn for rounds 1..k, stacked, to show progress across iterations.

kinds.definition: Makes an abstract idea visible without drawing the system: a geometric picture (manifold, contour landscape, embedding space, vectors, methods' trajectories in a space), a formal diagram (graphical model, automaton, derivation chain, game structure, matrix decomposition), an analogy scene, or a phenomenon shown on a few examples or an annotated curve. The reader gets the intuition or formal structure behind the method.

variants.definition: A formal object drawn in its own notation: graphical model with plates, automaton, derivation chain of boxed claims, game square, matrix or tensor decomposition.
A space made visible: manifold and charts, contour landscape, vector construction, distributions being transported, methods' trajectories compared inside the space.
The idea is shown happening on a few concrete examples (photos, toy scenes, quiz items) or on an annotated curve, with call-outs where it occurs.
A human, brain or everyday analogue drawn beside or instead of the method (stick-figure runner, human memory, human-written description).

kinds.definition: Maps a space so the reader sees its extent and structure: the tasks, categories, domains or data sources a benchmark, dataset or general model covers, or the family of prior methods and where the work sits. Drawn as a gallery of example cards, a taxonomy (tree, sunburst, radial genealogy, nested sets), a hub with spokes, or a dashboard combining these with statistics.

variants.definition: A grid of titled cards, one per task, category or domain, each with a real sample and its prompt or answer.
A tree, sunburst, radial genealogy or nested containment of categories, methods or theoretical classes, sometimes with example cards around it.
A dataset or benchmark summarised by a taxonomy plus statistics charts and examples in one composite.
A central artifact with its sources, domains or features arranged around it.

kinds.definition: The method as a cast of actors (agents, users, environment, tools, server and clients, cloud and device) and the messages, actions and feedback they exchange. The reader learns who does what and how the exchanges repeat, rather than following one input-to-output path.

variants.definition: Several agents with roles: a hierarchy, teams, a debate, or a supernet of agent operators.
One agent with its environment, tools, memory or user, exchanging in a loop or arranged as a hub.
Parties of different kinds (agent and user, cloud and device, server and clients) exchanging messages, control or model updates.

kinds.definition: Figure 1 is organised as separate tiles or titled sections, each carrying one contribution, finding, capability or deliverable of the paper (a headline number, a mini chart, sample outputs, a mini schematic, a small pipeline), rather than one drawing of the method. The tiles are read as a list of what the paper offers; no process runs through them. A tile may itself be a small pipeline, model or comparison, and then the figure carries that kind as well.

variants.definition: A grid of tiles of unequal size, each a highlight (headline number, mini chart, sample output, mini schematic), usually around a title or logo tile.
Sections titled by the paper's parts or sections, each summarising what that part contributes; the figure is a map of the paper.
Two to four panels, one per deliverable of the paper (task, dataset, model, benchmark, framework), each drawn in its own way.
Cards that each show one thing the system can do on a real example, sometimes with a summary chart; the method itself is not drawn.
One panel per finding or claim, each with its own small plot or schematic and a one-line takeaway.

tags.definition: One colour per group (view, client, task, modality, chunk) is kept on every element that belongs to it - inputs, intermediate blocks, outputs, legend rows, even the matching terms of a formula - so each group can be followed across the figure. The same device ties two distant elements that correspond - a claim and the panel that backs it, a prompt word and the mask it asks for, a graph region and the code lines written for it - by one shared colour in place of an arrow.
Wide block arrows (hollow, filled or gradient-filled, sometimes holding a word) or large chevrons carry the hand-over between stages, panels or results, set apart from the thin arrows of data flow.
A large language model as a box, logo, robot or mascot.
Spans inside sample text (prompts, answers, captions, reasoning, documents) are coloured, shaded or underlined to mark categories, evidence, key words, edits or errors.

A row or grid of identical small panels - thumbnails, plots or graphs - that differ in one factor (step, noise level, time, strength, topology, case or method), so the eye compares along the row or down the column.
Whole outputs, lanes, candidates or claims carry a verdict: a check or cross, thumbs, a happy or sad face, a short verdict word, or a red versus green tint of the lane.

A sequence drawn as a row, or stacked rows, of small token cells or chips coloured by role, modality, score or mask state, with brackets, arcs or lines showing grouping, alignment, attention or edits.
A model is drawn as a stock pictogram - a cartoon robot head that can show a mood, or a small node-and-edge network glyph - instead of a labelled box, a vendor logo or a named mascot.

Part of the figure is enlarged in an inset tied back to it by dashed leader lines, a cone or a magnifier: a block expanded into its internals (possibly over several levels), or a boxed image region magnified into a crop. The inset may also be tied to its source only by a shared colour and the repeated name, without a connector.

The figure, or a strip of it, states the task rather than the method: example inputs and the desired or produced outputs, the learning setting or data split, with the model absent or drawn as one black box.

Arrow colour or line style tells kinds of flow apart - forward versus backward (gradient), training versus inference, clean versus unlabelled, main versus auxiliary, blocked gradients - explained by a key of sample arrows or by labels on the arrows.
Titles or names are written rotated by 90 degrees (or as stacked letters): band titles along the left edge, names inside tall narrow module boxes.

Module states - frozen versus trainable, active versus idle, quantised versus full precision, optional versus base - are coded by fill colour, greying, hatching or dashed outlines with a key, including the same blocks redrawn once per phase or variant with the state changing. Removed, pruned or switched-off elements left in place as faded ghosts are the same device.
A card or stack of thumbnails with counts standing for a dataset.
A real company, product, model or database logo (OpenAI, Llama, Gemini, GitHub, Wikipedia, ClinVar) used as the icon or node for a model, tool or data source.

A dataset, batch or set of samples, tasks or languages drawn as an offset or fanned stack of overlapping cards, pages or frames instead of a single box. The same offset copies behind a module, head, layer or worker say 'several of these'.
Vector marks are drawn on top of a photo, render, map or screenshot to show what the method sees or does there: boxes and masks, paths and arrows, axes, cursor traces, coverage regions, labels.
The prompt given to a model drawn as a text box, a card or a stack of text blocks whose slots or sections (task description, demonstrations, history, query, placeholders) are highlighted.
One dataset or benchmark record drawn in full with its labelled fields - the sample, its prompt or question, labels, evidence, metadata, verdict - to show what an entry contains.

Stages or blocks are stated by their equations: boxes whose content is a formula, or a formula printed beside or in a callout from each block, lane or column, so the method reads as a derivation. Bare symbols or tensor shapes printed beside every module or signal, tying the drawing to the method's equations, are the light form of it.
An exchange drawn as speech bubbles or turn boxes with speaker avatars, one per turn, tinted or outlined by speaker; several systems' answers may sit in columns aligned turn by turn.
The figure carries the paper's own branding: its title or product name as a header, a row of project links (code, data, homepage), or the system's logo or mascot as the central hub of the composite.
A network, encoder, tokenizer or compressor drawn as a trapezoid (or a funnel) that narrows in the flow direction, saying 'this maps many to few' without opening the module.
A dataset, corpus, memory or knowledge store drawn as a database cylinder (or a stack of them), named and sometimes sized, coloured by data type or split into parts.

A weight, similarity, score or mask matrix (or a stacked tensor) drawn as a small grid of cells whose fill pattern or colour carries the message - sparsity, pruning, low rank, sharing, masked patches, heat values - possibly joined by operator signs into a picture of a formula.

Curly braces, square brackets or tall parentheses gather several items - stacked prompt blocks, a run of thumbnails, a span of text, the inputs of a model - and name the group or hand it on as one arrow.
Video drawn as a film strip: a row of consecutive frames, possibly inside a sprocket-hole border, one row per prompt, method or clip.
A question or task card with model answers, ticks and crosses.
Snowflake / fire, padlock or a colour key on modules.

Iteration or feedback is drawn as one long return arrow from a late stage or the output back to an early stage or the input, usually around the outside of the figure and labelled with the round, the condition or the signal fed back.
One item drawn twice, before and after an edit or treatment - an image tile, a text answer, a matrix, a record, a network - side by side or stacked and joined by an arrow that names the change.
Small circles on the arrows carry an operator - plus, times, element-wise product, concatenation, sigma, a letter - where signals are summed, multiplied, gated or reduced.

A sketch of an embedding, latent or feature space - a plane, blob or sphere with a few coloured points, clusters or thumbnails, decision regions or a boundary, and push, pull or movement arrows - showing what a module or an objective does to the representation.

A strip, pill or panel heading inside the figure states a full sentence - the headline claim, a per-panel takeaway, a research question or a plain caption of what to notice - instead of a component label. Panel titles that are short selling points (Large Scale, High-Quality, Diverse) rather than component names count as well.
A block with attention and feed-forward sub-blocks, often stacked "xN".

Pictograms carry the statement instead of labelled boxes: a chain of captioned icons for the stages, or icons joined by plus and equals signs (possibly with counts) that state the method as an equation.

Concrete toy values - small numbers in matrix cells, bit strings, probabilities, a mini data table with missing cells - are written into the method's own boxes so an operation can be followed by hand.
A neural network drawn as columns of circular neurons joined by lines (all-to-all or sparse), often shrunk to a small glyph that stands for 'a model'.
A panel, card or block carries its title, letter or number on a small tab attached to a corner or edge of its frame, like a file-folder tab.

A cartoon character - an animal, creature, figure or characterful robot, possibly the paper's named system - personifies a model, agent or role, is reused across panels and may change expression or props.

A chain from noise to a clean sample with forward and reverse arrows; also a noise picture, a solver or denoiser box and the generated sample, or blobs of a noise and a data distribution joined by transport arrows (flow matching).
A loss drawn as a node with dashed or coloured arrows flowing back to what is trained, or as a double-headed arrow named by the loss between a prediction and its target.
The drawing departs from flat vector boxes: isometric pseudo-3D cubes and slabs, hand-sketched strokes, painterly or 3D-rendered (possibly AI-generated) scenes, or pixel-art sprites.
Encoder and decoder as boxes or trapezoids narrowing towards a latent.

The same object - a graph, list, table, matrix, token row or rendered scene - is redrawn after each step at the same scale, with only what changed recoloured, added or faded, so the procedure can be followed by eye.

A plot-shaped sketch with no measured data: named axes without ticks holding an illustrative curve, a 2x2 quadrant of regimes, methods placed at qualitative positions or regions, or a spectrum arrow whose poles name the extremes.
A framed key inside the figure defines the paper's symbols or the operator glyphs (circled plus, times, concat, softmax) so the drawing itself can be labelled with bare symbols.
The wrong part of an output is marked in place: a red dashed box or circle on an image region, a red-tinted span or step inside an answer, or a short tag naming the error pinned beside it.
Each stage, decision or factor is drawn as a menu of options (chips, cards, option columns, decision nodes) rather than one chosen component, mapping a design space or the axes a study varies.

A cloud-shaped bubble trailing small circles to an agent, user or model holds what it thinks, imagines, intends or remembers: the typed outputs of a step, an imagined exchange, pictograms of intent, a gloss of what codes mean.
Audio drawn as a waveform strip (sometimes turned upright as centred bars) standing for speech or a sound track, next to or under the frames, tokens or spectrogram it belongs to.
Observe / think / act (or plan / act / reflect) as a cycle around an agent.
Self- or cross-attention drawn as a block or as lines between tokens.
Agent and environment exchanging action, state and reward.

Costs or scores are drawn on each lane, design or output - run time with a clock, FLOPs or step counts, memory, coin stacks for budget, rows of icons as scores, a metric pill or a number printed on each render, a small metrics table or bar chart beside each schematic - so efficiency or quality is part of the comparison.
A 3D point cloud, mesh or Gaussian-splat render.
An agent calling tools, APIs or other models, drawn as icons around it.
Positive pairs pulled together, negatives pushed apart, or a similarity matrix.
A monospace listing of real code, JSON or test code drawn as a box, card or editor window and treated as data - generated programs, code samples, diffs passed between stages.
A person is drawn as an actor inside the workflow who inspects, corrects, approves, labels or gives feedback on an intermediate result, not only as the source of the input.
Measured plots carry drawn annotations that state the finding: shaded regime bands, dashed highlight boxes, bold take-away words, gain arrows.
Labels, notes or whole cards are tied to the exact spot of a picture, chart or drawing they speak about by thin leader lines, often in the card's own colour.
A small bell curve, peak or bar histogram attached to a model output, token or loss arrow to show the distribution being matched, reshaped or compared.
A titled storage box of past items (feedback, exemplars, knowledge entries) tied to an LLM or agent by paired retrieve and update arrows.
A small MLP, linear layer or projection head.

A ring chart of categories: a donut of shares or a two- to four-ring sunburst running from top-level groups to leaf tasks, with labels rotated along the sectors and often a logo or name in the hole; the coverage picture of a benchmark or dataset.
Panels, cards or zones are headed by a filled pill, chip or band that carries the title (often with the panel letter), usually in the panel's own colour.
Part of an image, spectrogram, patch grid or sequence is covered by grey, black or hatched blocks to mark what is masked, to be predicted, generated or edited.

The method or its parts are told through a drawn analogue - an everyday object or scene (a prism, gold mining, a river confluence, a character rolling down a loss curve) or the biological structure the model mimics - beside or instead of literal boxes.

Positive and negative samples (anchor / positive / negative, chosen / rejected, win / lose, A versus B) are drawn as colour-coded pairs and carried into the loss or verdict that pulls them together or pushes them apart.

An LLM or agent run drawn as an ordered sequence of typed blocks - think, plan, tool call with arguments, tool response, answer - each tagged by type, in a lane, a numbered call list or a thought bubble, possibly forking into parallel threads.
Ordered capability or difficulty levels (L0-L5, Bloom-style) drawn as a ladder, staircase or stacked pyramid of tiers, each tier extended with tasks, models or scores.
Several agents as avatars wired by message arrows or a topology.
A frame's title is set into a gap of its border line, like a fieldset legend, instead of sitting inside or above the frame.
The proposed part is drawn in a saturated accent while the prior method, the baseline or the existing parts stay grey, pale or black and white - in the diagram or in the result bars.
Every box, card or panel title carries a small icon that names its concept, so the boxes read as captioned pictograms.

A residual or skip path drawn as a line that leaves before a block, arches around it and rejoins after it, usually in a circled plus; also layer skipping or looping drawn as arcs over a row of layers.
An attention pattern shown as a heat map over an image or as a token-by-token grid; the two drawn forms are the parts saliency-heatmap and attention-mask-grid.
A node-link graph: with message passing between nodes, as a small glyph standing for graph data, or as one worked problem instance.
A query going to a database cylinder or index and coming back with items.
A feature, embedding or hidden vector drawn as a short row or column of cells, circles or bars, coloured by source, type or value.
Two halves of the figure are drawn as mirror images - two branches, modalities, lanes or loops - with matching parts at matching positions and the links between them at the centre.
The figure shows only the problem - limitations or failure modes of existing methods, a shortcut, a degradation or a hard case staged on concrete examples - and does not draw the remedy.
A vision-language model: image and text encoders feeding a language model.
A loop drawn as a closed ring: arrow segments, chevrons or icons around a centre (an agent, a mascot, a miniature of the system), one per step or role, read clockwise.
Who attends to whom, drawn as a token-by-token grid of filled cells (causal triangle, blocks, bands, evicted cells, measured attention weights) or as fans of lines between two token rows.

Small badges pinned to the edge or corner of a block, card or icon mark its status or where something applies: New / Optional pills, a tool icon on the components a method changes, an 'improved' badge on a retrained model, a circled abbreviation defined in the legend.

A frozen weight block with a low-rank side branch (A, B) added to it, or an adapter module slotted into a frozen stack; the update drawn as small matrices joined to the pretrained weight by a plus sign.
An attention, saliency or relevance heat map of an image, painted translucently over the photo or render or shown as a tile beside it, per layer, step or method.
A module, model or option that serves several columns, cards, stages or phases is drawn once as a bar or band spanning all of them, instead of being repeated in each.
A desktop, browser or phone screen - a real screenshot or a drawn mock window - that serves as the environment an agent observes and acts on, or as a gallery of tool interfaces.
A radar (spider) or radial bar chart of per-benchmark or per-dimension scores, one polygon per method, embedded in an overview, teaser or agent figure.
A tree of candidate states, thoughts or token sequences expanded by a search (MCTS, beam search, tree of thoughts), with scores or values at nodes, possibly redrawn once per search phase.
The evaluator - an LLM judge, a human expert, an auditor or a reward that compares outcomes - drawn with courtroom props: a gavel, a judge's robe, a balance scale.
An environment drawn top-down as a floor plan, maze or grid world: walls, doorways, start and goal cells, objects as glyphs, sometimes a route or camera cones.
Two models drawn as teacher (expert, EMA copy) and student, linked by distillation, consistency or EMA arrows, with the teacher supplying targets or pseudo-labels.
Readout taps on a drawn model - probe glyphs or arrows from several layers to a linear probe, LM head or logit lens - showing where internal states are read.
Encoder, latent or discrete codebook, decoder.
Row labels in the left margin name aligned rows that run across several columns, panels or cases, so the figure reads as a matrix of rows by columns.
Cameras or views drawn in the scene: frustum pyramids along a camera path, view thumbnails tied to an object by rays, translucent cones or polygons for what each view covers.
The steps or stages are narrated in words outside the drawing: numbered caption boxes beside it, a caption strip along the bottom with one 'Step N' note per column, or bullet lists beside each stage.

Step-by-step reasoning drawn as a chain: Input, Thought, Thought, ..., Output boxes joined by arrows, the thoughts being text (or pictures), or a block of placeholder reasoning lines before the answer.
Successive model checkpoints (theta0 to thetaT, first to final reference model) drawn as a chain along one edge, with the data or data split that feeds each hop.
A ruled table comparing methods or examples row by row against named columns - capabilities, criteria, formulas - with check and cross marks, numbers or small drawings in the cells.
Convolutional layers as slabs or a pyramid of feature maps.
An image cut into a grid of patches that become tokens.
An objective drawn as a surface or as contour lines - a 3D bowl, hills and valleys, a tilted plane - with a descent path or one trajectory per method from a shared start.
The size of a repeated glyph or card carries a quantity: the same icon at growing sizes for model strength or cost, circles shrinking with a count, cards growing taller with difficulty.

Lanes per device, worker, pipeline stage, request or session along a time or step axis, holding coloured work blocks, memory bars, idle or padded gaps and transfers - the Gantt-style schedule of systems and efficiency figures. Coloured bars along a time axis that give the span of each event under a film strip belong here too.
An algorithm, pseudocode or API listing placed inside the figure that states the method (or how to call the library) in code or numbered steps, beside or linked to the drawn parts.

Each generated output is shown with the condition that produced it: a small glyph or inset (orientation cube, layout boxes, pose, sketch) on the output, or spans of a strip marked as condition versus generated.
A knowledge, commonsense or scene graph drawn as entity or object nodes joined by edges that carry relation names; also single (head, relation, tail) triples.
Two encoders drawn in parallel - one per modality, view or tower, sometimes sharing weights - whose outputs meet in a similarity, alignment or contrastive block.
A hierarchy of categories, criteria, tasks or design choices drawn as a tree - a root, branch boxes and leaf boxes or thumbnails - or nested by curly braces.
A ranked table of models with scores: rank badges or medals for the top rows, a logo or icon per model, bars or arrows for score and rank change.
A server and clients exchanging model updates.
The U-shaped encoder-decoder with skip connections.
A few-shot episode drawn as a support set (a few labelled samples) and a query set (one or two samples) entering the same model, which answers for the query.
Measured 2-D projections (t-SNE, UMAP, PCA) of learned features, coloured by class or domain, one panel per method or branch for comparison.
A dated axis with prior methods and the proposed one hung along it, grouped by family, placing the work in a line of research.
A theoretical or model-predicted curve or pattern is placed beside measured data on matching axes, so the reader checks that they agree.
